tasks.subject: fix(cli): keep the event log whole when several processes rotate it
tasks.prompt_intent:
fix(cli): keep the event log whole when several processes rotate it

A writer kept its descriptor and its own count of the file's size for
life, and several processes append to one store. After another process
rotated twice, a long-lived writer's descriptor named a file with no
path: its writes succeeded and went nowhere, so a daemon stopped
appearing in `kivgraph logs` until it restarted. After one rotation by
someone else, a writer's stale count rotated the fresh, nearly empty
file over the full rotation, discarding the history one rotation is
kept for. And writers that each stayed under the limit by their own
count passed it together.

tasks.subject: fix(hook): leave a search over files the graph does not cover
tasks.prompt_intent:
fix(hook): leave a search over files the graph does not cover

The gate asked the graph about the pattern alone and never read where
the search was looking. A bare word that two symbols declare was
refused whatever the target: …, a grep of
a log, a glob over YAML. The caller was told to call find_references
for a JSON key, and from the native Grep tool the printed escape -- a
variable before the command -- cannot be applied at all.

tasks.subject: fix(mcp): spend the find_by_intent candidate bound where it matters
tasks.prompt_intent:
fix(mcp): spend the find_by_intent candidate bound where it matters

The bound was spent in the order the question was written and before
repo, kind and path_prefix applied. A word most of the graph carries
filled it with whatever sorted first, so the symbols a rarer word named
never became candidates; and a narrowing that selected symbols past the
first few thousand matches came back empty, with guidance that blamed
the narrowing for excluding what was never looked at.

tasks.subject: fix(mcp): match a selector's path as a file or a directory
tasks.prompt_intent:
fix(mcp): match a selector's path as a file or a directory

The `path` of a symbol selector was applied as a string prefix. The
exact path of one file also matched every file whose name starts the
same way -- … beside … -- so naming the file could
not separate them and the answer was AMBIGUOUS_SYMBOL with only a
stable key offered as the way out. A path cut short in the middle of a
name resolved as if it were whole.

tasks.subject: fix(mcp): leave a root's members out of reached and of max_nodes
tasks.prompt_intent:
fix(mcp): leave a root's members out of reached and of max_nodes

trace_dependencies starts a container's walk from the root and its own
members, because a member is content and not a dependency. Two counts
still treated the members as reached: `reached` was every visit but
one, so a class with nine methods reported nine symbols it does not
reach, and the seeds counted against max_nodes, so a budget below the
member count was refused as INVALID_ARGUMENT.

tasks.subject: fix(indexing): watch around a source file that cannot be read
tasks.prompt_intent:
fix(indexing): watch around a source file that cannot be read

One path that existed and could not be read failed the whole batch in
the content hasher: every other change in it was discarded, the cache
was not updated, and each periodic reconciliation failed the same way
for as long as the path stayed unreadable. At startup the same failure
ended the source watcher, and with it every later invalidation of the
profile.

tasks.subject: fix(storage): reclaim candidates a dead rebuild left behind
tasks.prompt_intent:
fix(storage): reclaim candidates a dead rebuild left behind

A rebuild that is killed leaves `<id>.tmp` in the generation store.
Publish reclaims the one whose id it is about to reuse, and nothing
else ever looked: after a `clean` the numbering restarts, the id is
never reused, and a partial database stayed on disk while `clean`
reported everything removed.

tasks.subject: fix(indexing): ignore vendor only beside a dependency manifest
tasks.prompt_intent:
fix(indexing): ignore vendor only beside a dependency manifest

The watcher and its reconciler ignored every directory named `vendor`,
in every language. A source directory with that name -- … in a
TypeScript, Python, Java, C# or Dart repository -- fired no event and
was never hashed, so its edits never reached the graph, while discovery
and the tree digest treated the same files as source.

tasks.subject: fix(mcp): bind a cursor to include_derived
tasks.prompt_intent:
fix(mcp): bind a cursor to include_derived

find_references, find_symbol, get_blast_radius and trace_dependencies
hashed their query without include_derived on the single-profile path,
although the flag changes which rows the answer holds. A cursor minted
with one value was accepted with the other and applied its offset to a
different set, so rows were skipped or repeated with no error. It is
now CURSOR_INVALID, as it is under any other changed filter. The field
is omitted when false, so cursors minted without the flag still resume.

tasks.subject: fix(mcp): fail get_source when no selected profile holds a symbol
tasks.prompt_intent:
fix(mcp): fail get_source when no selected profile holds a symbol

Across profiles a selector that resolved nowhere was skipped, so a
misspelt or unindexed symbol read as one body fewer, and a call where
none resolved answered with zero bodies and no error. The single
profile path returns SYMBOL_NOT_FOUND, and so does every other
cross-profile tool. A symbol missing from one profile and present in
another is still served.

tasks.subject: fix(storage): hold the publish lock for restore, prune and discard
tasks.prompt_intent:
fix(storage): hold the publish lock for restore, prune and discard

Only Publish took the cross-process lock. It reads CURRENT, builds for
minutes and then writes both pointers, so a rollback made meanwhile
reported PASS and was overwritten when the rebuild finished; a prune or
a clean could remove a generation the publication was about to name.
Restore, Prune, Discard and DiscardExcept now take the same lock and
lose with ErrPublishInProgress, changing nothing.

tasks.subject: fix(mcp): key the get_source file cache by repository
tasks.prompt_intent:
fix(mcp): key the get_source file cache by repository

The per-call cache was keyed by the repository-relative path, so two
symbols in different repositories that share a path -- main.go,
… -- were both cut from whichever file was read first. The
answer named one repository and carried the other's code with
fresh:true, and a line range past the end of the cached file panicked
with a slice out of range.
